description: Synthetic meeting notes across industries with hand-labelled gold items. All people and organisations are fictional. Gold items match a prediction when the prediction's text + quote contains every keyword (case-insensitive). 'forbidden' strings must not appear in any extracted item.

cases.notes:
Attendees: Bea Ellwood (Highways), Jonah Thorne (Parish Council); Olive Grant, Cara Mendes.

1. Marlow Fen alignment
Bea Ellwood confirmed the council will not oppose the preferred alignment provided hedgerow loss is offset within the parish. The eastern option is no longer under consideration. We will share the hedgerow replanting plan by 6 November.

2. Construction hours
Jonah asked whether viaduct pours could avoid Sundays. Cara said we will revise the working hours proposal to exclude Sundays before the next liaison meeting.

3. Traffic
Olive will send the haul route drawings to Bea by Friday.

Clinical governance review — Riverside Trust
Present: Dr Priya Nair (Medical Director), Tom Okafor (Patient Safety Lead); Hana Lewis, Marcus Bell.

The board approved the pilot of the new discharge checklist on two wards from 1 October.
Dr Nair agreed to nominate a clinical champion for each ward by 25 September.
Hana will circulate the revised audit template to the ward managers by Friday.
Tom raised concerns about staffing over winter; no decision was taken on additional bank shifts.
It is still unclear whether pharmacy can support same-day discharge on weekends.

Community benefit fund — Cefn Ridge wind farm
Attendees: Gwen Harlow (Community Council chair), Ifan Pritchard (Landowner rep); Sam Ortiz.

It was agreed that the fund will be administered by the community council rather than a new trust.
Sam will draft the fund terms of reference and send them to Gwen by 17 August.
Ifan said the landowners will confirm access arrangements for the cable route next week.
Gwen asked if the annual contribution would be index-linked. Sam to check with finance.

Town centre regeneration — cabinet member briefing
Present: Cllr Ruth Adeyemi, Neil Barker (Head of Planning); Fatima Shah, Leo Park.

Cllr Adeyemi signed off the consultation plan for the market square proposals.
The pedestrianisation of Bridge Street was withdrawn from phase one.
Fatima will book the exhibition venue for the public drop-in sessions by 15 July.
Neil committed to providing the heritage impact assessment before the cabinet meeting.
Leo to update the project risk register.

Regulator engagement — quarterly supervisory meeting
Attendees: Alicia Romero (Supervisor), Ken Watanabe (Policy); Diane Fox (Compliance).

The regulator confirmed that the remediation plan timeline is acceptable.
We will submit the updated consumer duty board report by 30 June.
Alicia asked whether the complaints data could be broken down by product line.
Diane will arrange a follow-up session on operational resilience testing.
Ken mentioned the consultation on outsourcing rules may be published in the autumn.

Student accommodation partnership
Present: Prof Elena Rossi (Pro-Vice-Chancellor), James Kerr (Student Union President); Nadia Iqbal.

The university decided to cap first-year rent increases at 3% for 2027.
James will share the student survey results with Nadia by Thursday.
Nadia said we will publish the affordability framework in due course.
Prof Rossi asked whether the partnership covers postgraduate housing.

Enterprise customer steering call — Northwind Logistics
Attendees: Mei Chen (CIO, Northwind), Rafael Duarte (Procurement); Owen Price, Zara Ali.

Northwind approved the move to single sign-on for all depots.
Owen will send the SSO migration runbook to Mei by 30 April.
Zara agreed to set up a weekly status call during the migration.
Rafael asked if the renewal could move to a three-year term. Pricing remains open pending legal review.

Funder check-in — clean water programme
Present: Samuel Mensah (Programme Officer, funder), Laura Bianchi (Field Director); Grace Kim.

The funder endorsed the revised year-two budget.
Grace will provide the quarterly impact report by 31 March.
Laura agreed to host a site visit for the funder in May.
Samuel asked whether the monitoring data could be shared with partner NGOs.

Harriet Cole: Thanks for coming. The main thing for us is the lorry movements past the school.
Daniel Ross: Understood. We will move deliveries outside school drop-off and pick-up times from next month.
Harriet Cole: That would help. Can you put that in writing?
Daniel Ross: Yes, I'll send you a letter confirming the delivery windows by Monday.
Harriet Cole: And the noise monitoring results?
Daniel Ross: Those still need to be verified, so I can't promise a date yet.

Patient advocacy group engagement
Attendees: Dr Anke Vogel (Medical Affairs), Marta Silva (Patient Group CEO); Chris Doyle.

We agreed that the patient group will co-design the trial information leaflet.
Chris will share the draft leaflet with Marta by 20 February.
Marta will collect feedback from members over the following two weeks.
The group asked whether travel costs for trial participants will be reimbursed; this is to be confirmed by finance.
